question: For facility-064, resolve the historical Clean Harbors site and register the enforcement inventory dates separately from the associated inspection dates. Which records must be obtained before concluding correction or closure?
answer: The October 2013 index lists a March 14, 2011 notice concerning the July 16, 2009 inspection, an October 12, 2012 inspection report also concerning July 16, 2009, and an October 31, 2011 notice/certification concerning the August 25, 2011 inspection. Report and correspondence dates differ from inspection dates; a certification in a subject title does not establish agency acceptance, remedy completion or present closure. Obtain the original listed letters/reports and subsequent agency endpoint evidence. This packet acquires the index, not every item it inventories.

question: For facility-064, draft a diligence finding that combines the current EPA approval summary, historical enforcement inventory and the original 2024 inspection qualification. Does the 2025 renewal show every historical concern was closed?
answer: EPA reports an October 10, 2025 notice, no comments during the 30-day period, and a December 8, 2025 ten-year PCB storage approval. That is TSCA authorization history, while DTSC separately regulates hazardous waste under RCRA. The older index lists inspection-related noncompliance/correction correspondence, and the 2024 report expressly states its areas of concern were not compliance determinations. Neither current renewal, no public comments nor an indexed certification proves all past matters were finally resolved. Request actual enforcement endpoints and the separately qualified state permit; preserve the original namespace and date discrepancies.

evidence.quote: EPA regulates the handling of PCB waste at the Emerald Transformer facility under a Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) Approval (permit). The State of California’s Department of Toxic Substances Control, authorized under federal law, regulates the handling of hazardous waste under a Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) hazardous waste permit. EPA concluded in 2025, based on a thorough review of the permit application, that Emerald Transformer satisfies the TSCA requirements for storage of PCBs set forth in 40 CFR §761.65(d). EPA has also concluded that PCB operations at the Facility do not pose an unreasonable risk of injury to human health or the environment. On October 10, 2025, EPA issued a Public Notice announcing a 30-day public comment period on a Proposed PCB Commercial Storage Facility permit. No public comments were received during the public comment period. On December 8, 2025, EPA issued a Final PCB Commercial Storage Facility Approval (permit) to allow Emerald Transformer to continue storing PCB waste. That permit will be valid for 10 years. EPA also regularly conducts inspections of the facility to ensure that the existing permit conditions are being followed. Such inspections are unannounced and include random wipe sampling to check for residues and evidence of chemical releases.
